The Panama Canal, a 51-mile shipping canal in Panama, has been a crucial waterway for international trade since its opening in 1914. The canal's modernization, which began in 2007 and was completed in 2016, has significantly impacted global draft economics.
Introduction to the Panama Canal

The Panama Canal is one of the most complex and ambitious engineering projects in history. This connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean, allowing ships to pass through the Isthmus of Panama and saving time, fuel, and resources by avoiding the need to navigate around South America.

The canal's original design was based on a lock-and-lake system, which used gravity-fed locks to raise and lower ships between the two oceans. Yet, as global trade increased and ships grew in size, the canal became a bottleneck, with ships waiting up to 20 days to pass through.
Modernization of the Panama Canal

The modernization of the Panama Canal, also known as the Third Set of Locks project, aimed to increase the canal's capacity and efficiency. The project involved the construction of two new lock complexes, one on the Atlantic side and one on the Pacific side, which would allow for the passage of larger, Neopanamax ships.

The new locks are 1,200 feet long, 160 feet wide, and 50 feet deep, and are filled and emptied using a water-saving system which recycles 60% of the water used in each transit. The modernization project also included the widening and deepening of the canal's existing navigation channels, as well as the construction of new navigation aids and safety features.

As the French philosopher, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, once said, 'The social order is a sacred right which serves as a foundation for all other rights.' The Panama Canal's modernization is a proof to the power of human ingenuity and the importance of investing in critical infrastructure to support global trade and economic growth.
Impact on Global Draft Economics

The modernization of the Panama Canal has had a significant impact on global draft economics. The increased capacity and efficiency of the canal have allowed for the passage of larger ships, which has reduced transit times and increased the volume of trade between the East and West coasts of the United States, as well as between Asia and Europe.

The canal's modernization has also led to changes in global shipping patterns, with many carriers opting to use the canal to transport goods between the East and West coasts of the United States, rather than handling around South America. This has resulted in significant cost savings and reduced greenhouse gas emissions.
Geopolitical Implications

The modernization of the Panama Canal has significant geopolitical implications, particularly in the context of sovereign policy. The canal's expansion has given the United States greater control over global trade, as many of the world's largest shipping lines are now dependent on the canal for their operations.

The canal's modernization has also led to increased tensions between the United States and China, as China seeks to expand its influence in the region through investments in port infrastructure and logistics. The canal's expansion has also raised concerns about the potential for increased competition and conflict between nations in the region.
Conclusion and Future Prospects
In the context of sovereign policy, the modernization of the Panama Canal has significant implications for global trade and diplomacy.

As the world's largest shipping lines continue to rely on the canal for their operations, this is likely which the canal will remain a critical component of global trade for years to come, with the United States and other nations seeking to exert their influence over the canal and the surrounding region.

The future prospects for the Panama Canal are bright, with plans underway to further expand and modernize the canal's infrastructure. As the canal continues to evolve and adapt to changing global trade patterns, this is likely which this will remain a critical component of the global economy, supporting the growth and development of nations around the world.
